review.summary: Switching to `outside` with unconditional `padding-inline-start: var(--list-marker-gap)` gives every `List` extra left indent (previous behavior was `padding:0` unless `withPadding`) and puts markers in the padding box where they are easily clipped by `overflow:hidden`/tight containers, matching the screenshot’s indented text with missing/clipped bullets.

findings.title: Non-withPadding List now always indented – broken backwards compat
findings.explanation: Old `.root` was `list-style-position:inside; padding:0` and only added `padding-inline-start: var(--mantine-spacing-md)` when `data-with-padding`. New adds `--list-marker-gap` (`--mantine-spacing-lg`) unconditionally and `calc(marker-gap+md)` when padded. Plain `<List>` therefore shifts right by lg even when caller did not request offset. Screenshot shows plain list whose items are unexpectedly inset under the heading; existing layouts that aligned List flush-left regress.

findings.title: Outside markers clipped/hidden in constrained containers
findings.explanation: `list-style-position:outside` renders markers in the `padding-inline-start` area outside the content box. If any ancestor clips overflow (Card/Modal/Drawer/flex item with `overflow:hidden`, narrow `div style=padding:0` as in story) the disc/decimal is cut off. In screenshot no discs/decimals are visible – only indented text remains, with a faint black sliver at the very left edge being the clipped marker – while old `inside` never clipped.

findings.title: Icon/unstyled/listStyleType:none still reserves marker gap
findings.explanation: `.item[data-with-icon]{list-style:none}` hides the marker but `.root` still keeps `padding-inline-start:var(--list-marker-gap)`. Same for `listStyleType='none'` or `unstyled`. Result is an empty gutter where a marker would be, shifting icon-lists right with no marker to justify it. Fix should zero or not add the gap when markers are disabled; outside technique requires the padding to be conditional on having a visible marker.

review.summary: PR removes global CSS filter for dark-mode but leaves interactive-canvas filter, and ColorInput hex handling drops the leading `#` for 8-digit hex, producing invalid CSS colors that render as black (as seen in screenshot).

findings.title: Bare hex8 without `#` produces invalid color string
findings.explanation: normalizeInputColor only prepends `#` when tc.getFormat()==="hex". For 8-digit hex (hex8) like "ffec9980" it returns "ffec9980" without `#`. Rough/canvas fillStyle/strokeStyle with an invalid CSS value falls back to black, matching screenshot: picker shows #ffec9980 (light yellow 50%) while ellipse renders solid black. Old getColor("#"+c) always added "#".

findings.title: Interactive canvas still filtered causing double transform in dark mode
findings.explanation: Static canvas now uses JS applyDarkModeFilter per-element but .interactive keeps filter: var(--theme-filter). Any element drawn on the interactive layer (newElement, drag preview, selection decorations that reuse drawElementOnCanvas) will be filtered by JS and then again by CSS, producing incorrect colors / double inversion in dark mode. Either remove filter entirely and transform UI primitives individually, or ensure scene elements are never drawn on the filtered layer.

findings.title: Snapshot encodes buggy hex8 handling
findings.explanation: Test expects normalizeInputColor("ff000080") to stay "ff000080" without `#`, documenting the bug above as intended behavior and preventing future fix from being caught.

findings.explanation: When `config.progress` and `props.progress` are both undefined, `const mergedProgress = { ...config.progress, ...customProgress }` produces `{}` instead of `undefined`. `UploadList/index.tsx:48` only applies `progress = { size: [-1,2], showInfo: false }` when `progress` is `undefined`; an empty object bypasses it. `ListItem` then renders `<Progress percent={file.percent} {...progressProps}>` with default `showInfo=true` and default size, so every uploading item now shows the percentage text (e.g. "33%" in screenshot) and a larger bar, regressing prior behaviour where no progress prop meant a thin 2px bar without info.

review.summary: PNG export of arrows with bound text now paints an opaque/transparent rectangular hole on the shared export context instead of isolating the mask in a temp canvas. The hole erases any scene content already drawn (e.g. the pink container behind the label), turning a transparent arrow-gap into a solid canvas-background box as shown in the screenshots.

findings.title: Direct draw + clearRect/fillRect on export context erases underlying elements
findings.explanation: Old code drew the arrow into an offscreen tempCanvas scaled by appState.exportScale, clearRect-ed the label area there, then composited the tempCanvas with drawImage. Transparent pixels preserved whatever was already on the export context (the pink container/fill). New code draws the arrow vector directly onto the shared export context (with its current bootstrap scale/exportScale transform) and then does clearRect or fillRect with canvasBackgroundColor at holeX/holeY. That rect operation runs on the same context that already contains the container rectangles drawn earlier in staticScene, so it wipes the pink fill under the label. If viewBackgroundColor is opaque the code fills with renderConfig.canvasBackgroundColor (white) — producing the white box in screenshot 2; if transparent it clearRects to fully transparent. Neither matches the isolated-blit behavior which left the container visible through the arrow gap (screenshot 1/editor view). Fix needs an isolated layer, clip/mask, or destination-out that only masks the arrow stroke without affecting destination pixels, and must correctly handle rotation/exportScale.

review.summary: Description-only notices with an icon/type collide with the close button because the compensating CSS never matches.

findings.title: `&:first-child` on description never matches when icon is present, leaving no close-button reserve space
findings.explanation: PR removes the always-rendered `.notice-title` (which carried `.notice-closable .notice-title { paddingInlineEnd: paddingLG }`) and tries to compensate with `.notice-description { &:first-child { marginInlineEnd: marginSM } }`. In `PureContent` the icon (`<span class="*-icon">`) is rendered before title/description, so for `type="error|success|..."` / `icon` + `description` only, description is 2nd child, not `:first-child`, selector never applies. The closable-title rule also no longer applies because title is not rendered. Result is overlap/truncation of long description under the absolutely-positioned `.notice-close` button shown in both screenshots (screenshot 2 is `icon + description` only). Even without icon the reserve is `marginSM` vs previous `paddingLG`, so spacing is halved and still clips.

review.summary: Lowering `--tl-layer-canvas-in-front` to 250 and deleting the dotcom `399` override puts the `FollowIndicator` / cursor layer behind `.tlui-layout` so the 2px follow border is occluded by the header/panels — the screenshot's truncated orange left-edge and missing top-edge is that regression.

findings.title: canvas-in-front lowered below UI hides follow border/cursors
findings.explanation: --tl-layer-canvas-in-front changed 600→250 sits below .tlui-layout at 300 (new comment acknowledges “compete with UI layer”). .tlui-following-indicator is position:absolute inset:0 inside .tl-canvas__in-front so its 1000 is relative to that 250 stacking context and can never appear above any panel. After change top/side segments that intersect the header / helper-buttons are painted behind the panel’s solid background – seen in screenshot as orange border cut off at header and only left stub visible. Prior 600 and dotcom’s 399 intentionally kept border above panels for full-viewport outline.

findings.title: deleted dotcom 399 override that kept border above panels
findings.explanation: Removed `.tla .tl-container{--tl-layer-canvas-in-front:399}` which was the product-specific fix to keep following-indicator/cursors just above tlui-layout/300 but below menus/400. Deletion with base now 250 silently changes dotcom to behind-panels behavior with no replacement, breaking expected UX for Hackathon 2026/Projects follow flow shown.

findings.title: documented ordering ties menu-click-capture and canvas-in-front
findings.explanation: Comment claims watermark(200) < canvas-in-front(250) < menu-click-capture(250) < panels(300) but --tl-layer-canvas-in-front and --tl-layer-menu-click-capture both 250. Equality makes stacking depend on DOM order (fragile across refactors) and means dismiss overlay is not guaranteed above interactive InFrontOfTheCanvas elements. Should be distinct e.g. 260 vs 250.

review.summary: The refactor of `offsetSign` breaks stacking for `stackOffset="sign"`: the accumulators are reset to the original un-stacked value instead of the new stacked top, so stacked bars render too short (100 → 75 in the repro) vs `stackOffset="none"`.

findings.title: offsetSign accumulator regression causes incorrect stacked-bar heights
findings.explanation: PR changed offsetSign to use strict null checks but now does `positive = series1` / `negative = series1` where series1 is the pre-offset value (col[1] before mutation). It should accumulate `col[1]` (or `positive + value`) like offsetPositive does. For the repro data [0,50,25,0,25] (total 100) each successive positive layer resets the baseline, so the "sign" chart stops at ~75 while "none" (which still uses `positive = col[1]`) reaches 100. Fix by assigning `positive = col[1]` and `negative = col[1]`.

review.summary: Treating `''` as non-renderable is correct, but `Form` was special-cased to keep `help=""` as renderable (`isNonNullable && !==false`). That leaves a phantom empty `ErrorList`/`with-help` node mounted at all times (visible due to `filledKeyFullKeyList.length`), breaks the `hasHelp`-priority over `errors` and corrupts `ItemHolder` marginBottom/minHeight measuring, producing the overlapping error under the input shown in the screenshot.

findings.title: hasHelp still true for empty string, creates phantom help entity
findings.explanation: PR makes `isReactRenderable('')===false` but changes ErrorList to `isNonNullable(help)&&help!==false` which is true for `''`. `fullKeyList` then returns `[toErrorEntity('',...)]` with key='' and `visible=true` even when there is no help. It hides real `errors/warnings` (hasHelp prioritized) and leaves a zero-height collapse node that interferes with motion/scrollHeight; ItemHolder measures marginBottom against this phantom node causing the `minHeight`/`-marginBottom` compensation to be wrong, so validation messages like 'Please input your username!' render in a collapsed wrapper overlapping the input border as in the screenshot. Should be `isReactRenderable(help)` (or also check `help!==''`).

findings.title: hasHelp/hasError/wither plus with-help class polluted by empty string
findings.explanation: Same special-case as ErrorList. `hasHelp` true for `''` makes `hasError` true permanently, so `useLayoutEffect` measures marginBottom and `className` always includes `ant-form-item-with-help` even without help/errors. `FormItemInput` then mounts `ErrorList` via `marginBottom!==null` with empty content, reserving `minHeight` and `-marginBottom` offset incorrectly. On real validation the new error either is suppressed (ErrorList prefers help) or animates from a zero-height container, producing the overlap highlighted in the screenshot and mismatch with `FormItem/index.tsx:377` which uses truthiness (`help||errors`) and correctly treats '' as empty.

review.summary: CSS-var refactor breaks solid/ghost rendering – hard-coded fallback vars and silent ghost variant conversion make solid buttons appear as transparent outlined (dark wrapper showing through, blue text) and drops legacy compatible styles.

findings.title: Hard-coded fallback vars replace transparent defaults
findings.explanation: New genVariantStyle sets --ant-btn-border-color/#000, --text-color/#000, --bg-color/#ddd as defaults instead of transparent/none. Any button whose color+variant combo is not matched (e.g., legacy .ant-btn-primary markup, custom color strings, or momentary CSR gap) falls back to black border/grey background instead of old transparent baseline. The screenshot shows a Solid button rendered as transparent with blue text on the dark ghost wrapper – the solid background var did not resolve and transparent ghost bg is showing.

findings.title: Ghost solid silently changes public class to outlined
findings.explanation: Added memo converts ghost&&solid -> [color,'outlined'], changing DOM from ant-btn-variant-solid ant-btn-background-ghost to ant-btn-variant-outlined ant-btn-background-ghost (snapshot update). This is a breaking API/class-name change for users asserting selectors/styles on .ant-btn-variant-solid.ghost and breaks old ghost-solid intent where background remained ghost but variant stayed solid.

findings.title: Removed genCompatibleButtonStyle breaks legacy type usage
findings.explanation: Old genColorButtonStyle+genCompatibleButtonStyle styled bare .ant-btn-primary/.ant-btn-default etc. even without new color/variant classes. Removal means pages using manual <button class='ant-btn ant-btn-primary'> or cached HTML with only legacy type classes lose styling and fall back to #000/#ddd placeholders – not-handled input the old code supported.

review.summary: PR removes the CSS `filter: invert(93%) hue-rotate(180deg)` from the static canvas but did not make the grid theme-aware. Light grid colors (#ddd/#e5e5e5) are now drawn unchanged onto a correctly-darkened canvas, producing the high-contrast white-on-black grid in the screenshot.

findings.title: Grid lines not dark-mode adapted after removing CSS filter
findings.explanation: `GridLineColor.Bold/Regular` are hard-coded to light-theme values `#dddddd`/`#e5e5e5` and used unconditionally in `strokeGrid()` (lines 89,108). Previously the whole static canvas had `filter: var(--theme-filter)` (invert 93% hue-rotate 180deg) which automatically darkened the grid; the PR removes that filter from `.excalidraw.theme--dark canvas` (styles.scss) and switches element/background rendering to explicit `applyDarkModeFilter()`.
